title: Pirates get Luke Weaver from Mets to bolster bullpen, but it costs them: MLB trade grades
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Mets get: SS Sammy Stafura

Pirates get: RHP Luke Weaver

Mets: A-
Pirates: B+

It’s not Mason Miller or Adrian Morejón, but the Pirates probably landed the best reliever that will actually be moved at this trade deadline. A year after sending closer (and hometown kid) David Bednar to the Bronx, the Pirates have summoned Weaver from Queens to save their bullpen. He will bring much-needed stability to the late innings.

Weaver, a converted starter who found his footing in the Yankees bullpen, signed a two-year, $22 million deal with the Mets this past offseason. As one of my colleagues wrote in The Athletic’s trade deadline Big Board: “Little of David Stearns’ offseason overhaul of the Mets has worked, and Weaver is the reason this sentence starts with ‘little’ instead of ‘none.’”

Weaver, 32, has a 1.84 ERA and a 0.818 WHIP in 44 innings this season. Those are refreshing numbers for Pirates fans who have spent this summer watching the likes of Gregory Soto, Mason Montgomery and Yohan Ramírez attempt to hold leads late in games. The Pirates’ bullpen ranks 22nd in the majors in ERA (4.34) and 24th in WHIP (1.41). The Pirates traded for Camilo Doval over the weekend and could still use another leverage arm.

That Weaver’s addition costs the Pirates Stafura, a well-regarded position-player prospect, will sting. They wouldn’t have parted with him for a rental. But for one-plus years of Weaver, it is worth the cost in prospect capital to reinforce the bullpen with a playoff spot in sight. — Stephen J. Nesbitt

Mets: B
Pirates: B

When the Pirates offloaded Ke’Bryan Hayes last summer, the prospect they received in return was Stafura, a second-round pick in 2023 out of the New York City suburbs. Stafura has put together a big summer and clobbered the pitchers of the Class-A South Atlantic League. He graded out as the No. 9 prospect in Pittsburgh’s system, according to MLB Pipeline. That’s a pretty impressive return for Weaver, who has been solid for the Mets in 2026 after struggling with pitch-tipping for the Yankees in the second half of 2025.

Stearns continues to execute the trades he needed to execute. The 2026 season remains a disastrous one for the Mets. But at least the roster’s architect is doing what he must to repair things. None of these individual deals will move the needle. Stearns can only hope the overall haul of prospects provides a better base for the franchise. It’s a tall task for a floundering club. — Andy McCullough
